The graph of the first derivative $y={f}^{′}(x)$ of the function $f(x)$ intersects the $x$-axis at the points $x=-6,$ $x=-1,$ and $x=3,$ as shown above. Find all the values of $x$ where the slope of the function $y=f(x)$ is negative.

$x\in ($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)⋃(-1,$
{{field-3}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following:

- If ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ for all $x\in (a,b),$ then the slope of $f(x)$ is equal to zero on $(a,b).$

- If ${f}^{′}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b),$ then the slope of $f(x)$ is positive on $(a,b).$

- If ${f}^{′}(x)<0$ for all $x\in (a,b),$ then the slope of $f(x)$ is negative on $(a,b).$

From the above graph, we can see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is negative on the intervals $(-\infty ,-6)$ and $(-1,3):$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193353/assets/0d326b09364a5a8a02de62e0403fdd64978a61cd85268e8d4c6921e3f3bd6fab.png)

Therefore, the slope of the function $f(x)$ is negative when

$$
x\in (\,-\infty ,-6\,)⋃(-1,3\,).
$$
